recent_public_events.speech: Questions first. I want to know whether Dain needs help. Tonight we keep Iven warm and make sure nobody goes past that bench.
recent_public_events.action: Elara agrees to the morning inquiries, checks that Iven has a seat near the warmth, and leaves the cellar barrier in place.

summary.summary: The three travelers investigated the Crooked Lantern's cellar bell and rescued Iven, whose hand was trapped beneath a fallen rack. Torren identified a shutoff board, but Elara's first attempt and a later coordinated attempt both failed; its rotten handle broke and the cellar remained flooded. Arlen's attempt to retrieve Iven's satchel also failed, and the papers washed beyond reach. The party withdrew safely. Mara honored the promised supper and beds. Iven says the lost papers were wage receipts naming his absent brother Dain under the heading North Sluice Repairs; those claims remain unverified. The party agreed to cautious inquiries in daylight. No combat occurred. Seven software checks produced four successes and three failures.
summary.next_hook: Ask where North Sluice Repairs is, whether Dain worked there, and who can independently verify Iven's account. The route, worksite, employer, reasons for Dain's absence, and truth of the wage claim remain undefined.

payload.narration:
Morning opens outside the Crooked Lantern, with all three travelers together at its doorway. The rain has eased to a fine drizzle. A muddy lane runs between low buildings toward a stone bridge visible a short walk away; water can be heard beneath its arch.

Beside the tavern entrance, a person in a patched gray coat presses a fresh notice onto a wooden board. Its large lettering reads: “NORTH SLUICE REPAIRS — ENQUIRIES AT THE BRIDGE.” The person steps back to check that the paper holds, then notices the travelers. “Morning.”

The familiar heading is plainly visible. Whether it leads to anyone who knows Dain remains unanswered.

Morning opens outside the Crooked Lantern, with all three travelers together at its doorway. The rain has eased to a fine drizzle. A muddy lane runs between low buildings toward a stone bridge visible a short walk away; water can be heard beneath its arch.

Beside the tavern entrance, a person in a patched gray coat presses a fresh notice onto a wooden board. Its large lettering reads: “NORTH SLUICE REPAIRS — ENQUIRIES AT THE BRIDGE.” The person steps back to check that the paper holds, then notices the travelers. “Morning.”

The familiar heading is plainly visible. Whether it leads to anyone who knows Dain remains unanswered.

recent_public_events.action: Arlen crouches on the ledge and reaches for the satchel's shoulder strap, trying to lift the open bag without spilling its remaining papers.
recent_public_events.text: The wet strap parts in Arlen's hand. The bag turns under the grate and empties into the dark water beyond it. recent_public_events.speech: We're done down here. Iven first, Torren behind him. Arlen, come with me. Mara needs to know that board is broken.
recent_public_events.action: Elara gathers her rope and takes a position on the stairs to help Iven climb, leaving the broken board alone.
recent_public_events.text: Iven climbs past Elara using the sound steps. His hand is painful, but he can walk. The water continues below them. The broken handle comes away with Elara's rope; the board itself cannot be operated safely from the landing.

recent_public_events.speech: Mara! Your guest is coming up. He'll need clean cloth. And nobody else goes down until the water drops.
recent_public_events.action: Torren follows Iven to the upper steps with his recovered staff and calls to Mara for help.
recent_public_events.text: Mara appears at the top with folded linen. 'Iven?' She sets the cloth on the floor and reaches to steady him with both hands. Seeing the water on their clothes, she moves a chair away from the door to clear their path.

recent_public_events.speech: A bell that rings because somebody needs help. I can invoice that as an investigation. The plumbing is beyond our qualifications.
recent_public_events.action: Arlen climbs back to the others, makes sure nobody remains below, and lets Mara know the satchel was lost.
recent_public_events.text: All three travelers and Iven reach the tavern floor. Mara closes the cellar door and draws a bench across it. Iven sits beside the counter, his empty good hand resting on his knee. The bell is silent below them.

The four sit near the counter while Mara wraps Iven's hand in clean linen. Rain still brushes the shutters. The cellar remains flooded behind its blocked door, and the lost receipts remain lost. Mara places a pot of hot broth on the table. 'You found out what was ringing. Supper and beds, as promised.'

recent_public_events.speech: Thank you for the food. But next time, tell us someone might be down there. Why were you hiding him?
recent_public_events.action: Elara asks Mara directly about sheltering Iven while leaving him space to answer for himself.
recent_public_events.text: 'He asked for somewhere nobody would think to look,' Mara says. 'I gave him a dry corner. It was dry then. I didn't want strangers asking whose papers he had.' Iven nods. 'My request. Her mistake was thinking I left. Mine was trying to mend the drain alone.' Neither offers proof of who, if anyone, is looking for him.

recent_public_events.speech: I can write down what you remember. That won't replace the receipts. Your brother's name first, and the place printed on them. I'll mark this as your account, not proof.
recent_public_events.action: Torren opens his notebook and asks Iven for the exact names he remembers, distinguishing recollection from verified evidence.
recent_public_events.text: 'Dain,' Iven says. 'My brother is Dain. The heading was North Sluice Repairs. Seven days ago, wages collected beside his name. I didn't see him sign it. I don't know who did.' He stares at the page. 'I know how little that is without the paper.' Neither Mara nor anyone at the table can corroborate the receipt.

recent_public_events.speech: We can ask about a man and a worksite tomorrow. That isn't a promise to accuse anyone, break into anything, or wade through another cellar. And if it becomes a job, we agree the price before the drowning.
recent_public_events.action: Arlen accepts Mara's supper and offers to help make cautious inquiries in the morning, with explicit limits.
recent_public_events.text: Iven gives a tired nod. 'Questions would be more than I had this morning.' Mara puts bread beside the broth. 'Ask in daylight,' she says. 'The drain can wait for someone with a proper brace.' No fee or route has yet been agreed.

recent_public_events.speech: Questions first. I want to know whether Dain needs help. Tonight we keep Iven warm and make sure nobody goes past that bench.
recent_public_events.action: Elara agrees to the morning inquiries, checks that Iven has a seat near the warmth, and leaves the cellar barrier in place.
recent_public_events.text: Mara brings another dry cloth for Iven's hand. He has stopped shivering by the time the broth cools enough to drink. The bench stays across the cellar door. Beyond the shutters, rain conceals whatever roads and settlements lie outside.

recent_public_events.speech: Dain. North Sluice Repairs. Claimed wages, not confirmed wages. Those are our questions. The rest can remain blank until morning.
recent_public_events.action: Torren reads back the distinctions in his notes, agrees to cautious inquiries at dawn, and closes the notebook for the night.

recent_public_events.speech: Mara! Your guest is coming up. He'll need clean cloth. And nobody else goes down until the water drops.

Mara places a pot of hot broth on the table. 'You found out what was ringing. Supper and beds, as promised.'

recent_public_events.speech: Morning. Who should we ask for at the bridge? And are these repairs hiring? I like to learn what a job involves before discovering it waist-deep.

recent_public_events.speech: Thank you. One more question: do you know a man named Dain? His brother hasn't heard from him in a month. We're trying to find out whether he needs help.

The poster remains beside the notice. The bridge is still visible through the drizzle.
